account: Rori is an AI-powered conversational math tutor on WhatsApp, created by Rising Academies, an education network that runs schools in Ghana. Henkel (University of Oxford), Horne-Robinson (Rising Academies), Kozhakhmetova and Lee (J-PAL North America) report a preliminary evaluation in 11 Rising Academies schools in Ghana. The schools were randomly assigned at the school level, five to treatment and six to control. Students in grades 3–8 took a 35-question math assessment in early February 2023 (baseline) and late August 2023 (endline). Of the 637 students who took the baseline (336 treatment, 301 control), 477 took the endline. Treated students were given a phone for one hour a week during study hall to study math with Rori. Controls continued regular instruction. The first version of the preprint appeared on arXiv on 15 February 2024. In the second version, posted on 5 May 2024, the authors report an effect size of 0.36 (Cohen's d, p < 0.001) and a marginal cost of about $5 per student. The arXiv abstract still describes approximately 1,000 students in grades 3–9, two 30-minute sessions a week over 8 months and an effect size of 0.37. These figures do not match the body of the second version. In December 2024 a University of Ghana professor and two Rising Academies staff registered a 2025 follow-up pilot in government and low-cost private schools. The registry entry posts no results. By May 2026 Rising Academies reported that it was piloting Rori in government schools in Ghana's Eastern Region with World Bank support. It had extended the pilot by six months and was preparing a larger randomized trial in more than 100 public schools from September 2026.

Henkel (University of Oxford), Horne-Robinson (Rising Academies), Kozhakhmetova and Lee (J-PAL North America) report a preliminary evaluation in 11 Rising Academies schools in Ghana. The schools were randomly assigned at the school level, five to treatment and six to control. Students in grades 3–8 took a 35-question math assessment in early February 2023 (baseline) and late August 2023 (endline). Of the 637 students who took the baseline (336 treatment, 301 control), 477 took the endline. Treated students were given a phone for one hour a week during study hall to study math with Rori. Controls continued regular instruction. The first version of the preprint appeared on arXiv on 15 February 2024. In the second version, posted on 5 May 2024, the authors report an effect size of 0.36 (Cohen's d, p < 0.001) and a marginal cost of about $5 per student. The arXiv abstract still describes approximately 1,000 students in grades 3–9, two 30-minute sessions a week over 8 months and an effect size of 0.37. These figures do not match the body of the second version. In December 2024 a University of Ghana professor and two Rising Academies staff registered a 2025 follow-up pilot in government and low-cost private schools. The registry entry posts no results. By May 2026 Rising Academies reported that it was piloting Rori in government schools in Ghana's Eastern Region with World Bank support. It had extended the pilot by six months and was preparing a larger randomized trial in more than 100 public schools from September 2026.
